1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { Link as RouteLink } from 'react-router-dom';
4	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
5	import { ZimmProductName } from '../../atoms/zimmProductName';
6	import { ZimmProductPrice } from '../../atoms/zimmProductPrice';
7	import { ZimmIcon } from '../../atoms/zimmIcon';
8	import { ZimmSizeChipGroup } from '../zimmSizeChipGroup';
9	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../zimmSizeChipGroup';
10	import { CARD_SLOT } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';
11	
12	/**
13	 * Selector contract for a later step (the ZimmProductCard organism, SFCC-236 Step 6): stable
14	 * `data-card-slot` values on this component's own DOM so that organism's own recipe can target
15	 * these descendants for hover-reveal styling without reaching into implementation details.
16	 * Do not rename these values without updating that recipe too — mirrors the same contract
17	 * `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` documents for its own slots:
18	 *   - "content"   — the outermost element (this component's root).
19	 *   - "price"     — the price wrapper. Always rendered regardless of variation; the organism's
20	 *                   own CSS is what shows/hides it on hover per variation (see the `showBag`/
21	 *                   `showSizeChips` props below), not this component.
22	 *   - "sizeChips" — the size-chip-group wrapper (present only when `showSizeChips` is true).
23	 *                   Always rendered in the DOM per Figma's `hidden=true` default on the "Size
24	 *                   Selector instance" node — the organism's hover-reveal CSS is what handles
25	 *                   visibility, not this component's own recipe (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts).
26	 *   - "bag"       — the bag-button wrapper (present only when `showBag` is true). Added later
27	 *                   than the three above, for the organism's own mobile-breakpoint hide rule
28	 *                   (Figma: PLP/PDP's Mobile Card-content instances have the bag icon's `Icons`
29	 *                   frame `hidden="true"`; Desktop and Wishlist's own Mobile instance do not) — a
30	 *                   viewport-width concern, not a hover one, but the same
31	 *                   "this component always renders it, the organism's CSS decides visibility"
32	 *                   division of responsibility as the other slots.
33	 */
34	
35	// Same import base SFCC's own swatch-group/swatch.jsx uses for its `RouteLink`, and the same
36	// reasoning zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx already documents: a router `Link` delivers "URL updates
37	// without a full page reload" for real. Confirmed directly (no overrides/app/components/link/
38	// directory exists on disk) — there is no overrides/.../link equivalent to reuse instead.
39	const ProductNameLink = chakra(RouteLink);
40	
41	const messages = defineMessages({
42	  // Deliberately generic, not name-interpolated ("Add {name} to bag") — no such requirement was
43	  // given, and the visible product name already sits immediately to this button's left in the
44	  // same row, so the accessible name does not need to repeat it.
45	  addToBag: { id: 'product_card_content.bag.add_to_bag', defaultMessage: 'Add to bag' },
46	  // Figma node 40002163:41468 (Desktop, Hover, PLP/PDP, Unavailable=True) — an instance of the
47	  // shared CTA/Link atom (40001908:28374/40001908:28368) with its text swapped to "NOTIFY ME" in
48	  // this state. Authored here in sentence case, not literal caps, matching this codebase's
49	  // pattern of keeping translatable copy normal-case and letting the textStyle's CSS apply the
50	  // visual transform (see ZimmProductName's own normal-cased stories against `productNames`'
51	  // textTransform: 'uppercase') — `linkSm` was corrected to `textTransform: 'uppercase'` to
52	  // match (2026-09-03, theme/foundation/typography.ts), so this renders "NOTIFY ME" correctly.
53	  notifyMe: {
54	    id: 'product_card_content.notify_me.label',
55	    defaultMessage: 'Notify me',
56	  },
57	});
58	
59	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCardContent';
60	
61	/**
62	 * `ZimmProductName`'s own heading-level prop, read off the atom's real signature via a utility
63	 * type rather than a hand-typed duplicate union (typescript.md: "prefer utility types over
64	 * hand-rolled duplicate shapes... a hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
65	 * original changes"). Its type param is `'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'` — note this is NOT `'h2' | 'h3' |
66	 * 'h4'` as an earlier sketch of this component's contract assumed; see `headingLevel` below.
67	 */
68	type ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductName>['as'];
69	
70	export type ZimmProductCardContentProps = {
71	  /** The product's display name, rendered as the card's heading and link text. */
72	  name: string;
73	  /**
74	   * Heading level for the composed `ZimmProductName`, forwarded to it as `as`. Named
75	   * `headingLevel` here (rather than `as`) because this component is not itself polymorphic —
76	   * it always renders the same fixed element tree, it just hands the one real heading a level.
77	   * Typed as `ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel` (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`) to exactly match what that atom
78	   * actually accepts — a prior sketch of this contract assumed `'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4'`, which is
79	   * wrong on both ends: the atom has no `'h4'` at all, and it does accept `'h1'` (unlikely in
80	   * practice for a grid card, but not this component's place to forbid what the atom allows).
81	   */
82	  headingLevel: ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel;
83	  /**
84	   * PDP destination for the product name link. Not passed through `isSafeHref` — unlike
85	   * `ZimmNavItem`/`ZimmContactIconRow`'s CMS-sourced hrefs, this is an SFCC-generated product URL,
86	   * the same trust level `ZimmColourSwatch`'s own `href` prop already assumes.
87	   */
88	  href: string;
89	  /** Passed straight through to the composed `ZimmProductPrice`. */
90	  currentPrice?: string;
91	  /** Passed straight through to the composed `ZimmProductPrice`. */
92	  originalPrice?: string;
93	  /** Passed straight through to `ZimmProductPrice`'s own `isLoading`. */
94	  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
95	
96	  /**
97	   * Wishlist-only attributes line (colour + size as plain text), per the organism's
98	   * VARIATION_CONFIG (Step 6, not built yet) — this component only ever sees the resolved
99	   * boolean, never a variation name. When false the row is absent from the DOM entirely, not
100	   * merely visually hidden.
101	   */
102	  showAttributes: boolean;
103	  /**
104	   * Rendered only when `showAttributes` is true. Pass the plain colour value ("Ivory", not
105	   * "Ivory,") — the component itself appends the trailing comma when rendering, matching
106	   * Figma's own text-node structure (confirmed via get_design_context on node 40002187:58446:
107	   * the colour text node's own content literally includes the trailing comma, e.g. "Lilac
108	   * Sand,", not a separate punctuation node). See the `colourWithComma` derivation below.
109	   */
110	  colour?: string;
111	  /** Rendered only when `showAttributes` is true. */
112	  size?: string;
113	
114	  /** Renders the bag button (Figma "Icon_bag" — confirmed a bag action, not a wishlist star). */
115	  showBag: boolean;
116	  /** Disables the bag button (native `disabled`) when true. `onAddToBag` never fires in that state. */
117	  isUnavailable?: boolean;
118	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
119	
120	  /**
121	   * PLP-only size-chip picker, per the organism's config. Always rendered in the DOM whenever
122	   * true — Figma's `hidden=true` default on this slot is a hover-reveal CSS concern for the
123	   * Step 6 organism, not something this component enforces on itself. See the module docblock's
124	   * `data-card-slot="sizeChips"` note.
125	   */
126	  showSizeChips: boolean;
127	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
128	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
129	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
130	
131	  /**
132	   * True only when the caller has already resolved "unavailable AND a usable notify-me callback
133	   * exists" (the organism's job). This component still independently requires `onNotifyMe` to be
134	   * present before rendering anything — belt-and-braces, the same defensive shape
135	   * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `onRemove` + `removeLabel` co-requirement uses.
136	   */
137	  showNotifyMe: boolean;
138	  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
139	};
140	
141	/**
142	 * Molecule — the product-card text-content block: heading/link, bag action, wishlist-only
143	 * colour/size attributes, price, PLP-only size-chip picker, and an out-of-stock notify-me CTA.
144	 * Figma "Card-content" component set, node 40002109:26908 (Desktop 40002109:26906 / Mobile
145	 * 40002163:37103).
146	 *
147	 * Deliberately has NO remove/close button — that action lives entirely in
148	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `close` overlay (Step 4), positioned on the image, not here.
149	 *
150	 * Also deliberately has no badge slot, despite the SFCC-236 AC mentioning one for PLP/Wishlist.
151	 * An earlier revision of this paragraph claimed no Figma design existed for it at all — that
152	 * was wrong: the badge (Figma "Tag") does exist, confirmed present and identical across every
153	 * Size/Type variant checked. It just lives inside "Image Group", which is
154	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain, not this component's — so it was built there instead. See
155	 * that component's own docblock for the confirmed spec, and the organism's own docblock
156	 * ("Badge" note) for which variations actually show it.
157	 *
158	 * Composes `ZimmProductPrice` with `isLive={false}` unconditionally — this is the entire reason
159	 * that prop exists (SFCC-236 Step 3): a grid of these on a PLP must not mount dozens of
160	 * `aria-live` regions whose price never changes post-mount.
161	 */
162	export const ZimmProductCardContent = ({
163	  name,
164	  headingLevel,
165	  href,
166	  currentPrice,
167	  originalPrice,
168	  isPriceLoading,
169	  showAttributes,
170	  colour,
171	  size,
172	  showBag,
173	  isUnavailable,
174	  onAddToBag,
175	  showSizeChips,
176	  sizeChipValues,
177	  selectedSizeChipValue,
178	  onSizeChipSelect,
179	  showNotifyMe,
180	  onNotifyMe,
181	}: ZimmProductCardContentProps) => {
182	  const intl = useIntl();
183	  // `disabled`, not `isUnavailable` — matches `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s own `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`
184	  // key so that guard's exhaustive prop-combination walk actually exercises both the true and
185	  // false branch of `bagButton`'s disabled styling (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts's own
186	  // comment, and `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s identical `disabled` naming for the same reason).
187	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE, { disabled: isUnavailable });
188	
189	  // Both conditions required, matching the component contract exactly — not just `showNotifyMe`
190	  // alone, so an organism that sets the flag without wiring a real callback silently renders
191	  // nothing rather than an inert button.
192	  const showNotifyMeButton = showNotifyMe && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
193	
194	  // Figma renders the colour/size attributes line as ONE continuous phrase, not two independent
195	  // labels: the comma is baked into the colour text node's own content ("Lilac Sand,"), not a
196	  // separate punctuation element — confirmed via get_design_context on node 40002187:58446 (the
197	  // real Wishlist Card-content instance). Reproduced the same way here, on the colour value's own
198	  // rendered string (never as a static comma JSX node between the two spans), paired with
199	  // attributesRow's 2px gap (zimmProductCardContent.css.ts) for the "Ivory, M" breathing room —
200	  // verified by rendering the real Futura Round Medium caption style at actual size: the glyph
201	  // ink-to-ink gap the 2px flex gap produces here reads as a genuine (if slightly tighter than
202	  // full-prose) space, not as "Ivory,M" touching. Guarded against `colour` being falsy so a
203	  // caller omitting it (a contract violation, but not this component's job to enforce) still
204	  // renders nothing, rather than the literal string "undefined,".
205	  const colourWithComma = colour ? `${colour},` : colour;
206	
207	  return (
208	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.content}>
209	      <chakra.div __css={styles.nameRow}>
210	        <ProductNameLink to={href} __css={styles.nameLink}>
211	          <ZimmProductName name={name} as={headingLevel} />
212	        </ProductNameLink>
213	
214	        {showBag && (
215	          <chakra.div __css={styles.bagWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.bag}>
216	            <chakra.button
217	              type="button"
218	              __css={styles.bagButton}
219	              aria-label={intl.formatMessage(messages.addToBag)}
220	              disabled={isUnavailable}
221	              onClick={() => {
222	                // Belt-and-braces: the native `disabled` attribute already prevents the browser
223	                // from ever dispatching this click, but stating the invariant explicitly means a
224	                // reader doesn't have to recall that fact to trust onAddToBag can't fire while
225	                // unavailable. Same idiom as ZimmSizeChip's own onClick guard.
226	                if (isUnavailable) return;
227	                onAddToBag?.();
228	              }}
229	            >
230	              <ZimmIcon type="bag" aria-hidden />
231	            </chakra.button>
232	          </chakra.div>
233	        )}
234	      </chakra.div>
235	
236	      {showAttributes && (
237	        <chakra.div __css={styles.attributesRow} data-testid="card-content-attributes">
238	          <chakra.span __css={styles.colourText}>{colourWithComma}</chakra.span>
239	          <chakra.span __css={styles.sizeText}>{size}</chakra.span>
240	        </chakra.div>
241	      )}
242	
243	      <chakra.div __css={styles.priceWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.price}>
244	        <ZimmProductPrice
245	          currentPrice={currentPrice}
246	          originalPrice={originalPrice}
247	          isLoading={isPriceLoading}
248	          isLive={false}
249	        />
250	      </chakra.div>
251	
252	      {showSizeChips && (
253	        <chakra.div __css={styles.sizeChipWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}>
254	          <ZimmSizeChipGroup
255	            values={sizeChipValues ?? []}
256	            selectedValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
257	            onSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
258	          />
259	        </chakra.div>
260	      )}
261	
262	      {showNotifyMeButton && (
263	        <chakra.button
264	          type="button"
265	          __css={styles.notifyMeButton}
266	          onClick={onNotifyMe}
267	          data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}
268	        >
269	          {intl.formatMessage(messages.notifyMe)}
270	        </chakra.button>
271	      )}
272	    </chakra.div>
273	  );
274	};
275	
276	export default ZimmProductCardContent;

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	import { CARD_SLOT, HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY, DESKTOP_QUERY } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';
3	
4	/**
5	 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
6	 * arrows/indicator split — now a shared import from `zimmProductCardShared.ts` rather than each
7	 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
8	 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the
9	 * exact same media feature, on this shared root.
10	 */
11	
12	/**
13	 * A viewport-width gate, unrelated to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above — governs the PLP-only bag-icon
14	 * mobile hide (Fix D, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) below. Also a shared import from
15	 * `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, same reasoning as `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above: this and
16	 * `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own `root` padding step both need the identical `min-width`
17	 * gate, and a module-private copy in each file was exactly the drift risk this extraction removes.
18	 */
19	
20	type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
21	  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
22	   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */
23	  hoverRevealsPrice?: boolean;
24	  /** PLP + Wishlist — price is visible by default (Content's own natural rendering; no override
25	   *  needed for that half) and hides only once a hover-capable pointer hovers the card. */
26	  hoverHidesPrice?: boolean;
27	  /** PLP + Wishlist — the size-chip picker is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default
28	   *  and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card, in the same
29	   *  media-query gate as the price swap above so both engage together. */
30	  hoverRevealsSizeSelector?: boolean;
31	  /** Fix C — true whenever ZimmProductCardContent actually mounted a notify-me button
32	   *  (`isUnavailable && onNotifyMe`, computed once in index.tsx as `showNotifyMe`). Unlike the two
33	   *  flags above, the "hidden by default" half lives INSIDE `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, not outside it
34	   *  — see docblock point 4: a touch pointer must see notify-me unconditionally (confirmed via
35	   *  every Mobile Unavailable Figma reference), where price/the size-selector do the opposite. */
36	  hoverRevealsNotifyMe?: boolean;
37	  /** Fix C — true for a PLP/Wishlist card that would normally hover-swap to the size-selector
38	   *  (`config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector`) but is out of stock. Unlike every other flag here, this
39	   *  is not a pointer-type concern at all: the size-chip wrapper stays hidden permanently, in
40	   *  every state, on every device — see docblock point 4. */
41	  sizeSelectorUnavailable?: boolean;
42	  /** Fix D — PLP only (`VARIATION_CONFIG.plp.hideBagOnMobile` in index.tsx). A viewport-width
43	   *  concern, not a pointer-type one: hidden below `breakpoints.md`, visible from it up — see
44	   *  docblock point 5. */
45	  hideBagOnMobile?: boolean;
46	};

48	/**
49	 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
50	 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
51	 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
52	 * own by itself:
53	 *
54	 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
55	 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
56	 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
57	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
58	 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
59	 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
60	 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
61	 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
62	 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
63	 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
64	 *      Four separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
65	 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
66	 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
67	 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but four plain keys need no such
68	 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
69	 *      ONE of the four (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
70	 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
71	 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close`, `carousel`, and `media` are the three
72	 *      exceptions: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own recipe already positions each of them directly
73	 *      (`close` via `position: absolute, top: 0, right: 0`; `carousel` via `position: absolute,
74	 *      top: 50%, ...`; `media` — its own root — via `position: relative`), so each needs (and
75	 *      gets) only the z-index bump here:
76	 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
77	 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
78	 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
79	 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
80	 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
81	 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the
82	 *          round-2 Scorer PASS, which explicitly flagged that check as still outstanding, not by
83	 *          any automated pass). The lift rule used to target
84	 *          `'[data-card-slot="carousel"] button'` — the two arrow BUTTONS individually, each given
85	 *          its own `position: relative, zIndex: 1` — identical in shape to the `content button`
86	 *          rule above, and every jsdom test passed. A real click in a real browser still landed on
87	 *          the overlay, not the arrow. Root cause: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `carousel` part
88	 *          sets `transform: translateY(-50%)` (to vertically centre the arrow row against `slide`),
89	 *          and `transform` unconditionally creates a NEW stacking context on that element,
90	 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
91	 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles
92	 *          against the *other* arrow button, never against anything outside `carousel` (like the
93	 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
94	 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
95	 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
96	 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
97	 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
98	 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
99	 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
100	 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
101	 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
102	 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.
103	 *        - `media` — Fix I (SFCC-236, found via a real mobile-device touch-swipe check performed
104	 *          after this branch's own live testing round, not by any automated pass). The media/
105	 *          gallery scroll region itself was never added to this lift list, even though it is
106	 *          exactly as interactive as the controls nested inside it: with no z-index of its own,
107	 *          `[data-card-slot="media"]` sat at the same default/auto stacking layer the overlay
108	 *          itself occupies, so a touch swipe starting on the image landed on the invisible
109	 *          overlay `<a>` first and the real scroll container underneath never received the
110	 *          gesture — the slide indicator still rendered correctly (proving the image data/gallery
111	 *          logic was fine), but nothing paged. Missed earlier because `close`/`carousel`/content-
112	 *          buttons were each checked with a real CLICK (Fix 1, Fix 3 above) — and a click on the
113	 *          image happened to "work" by accident either way, since it also landed on the overlay
114	 *          `<a>` and still navigated to the PDP — so nothing about a plain tap ever surfaced this;
115	 *          only a real SWIPE (which needs the scroll container itself, not the overlay, to be the
116	 *          hit target) exposed the gap. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own root is already `position:
117	 *          relative` (its own recipe), so, same as `close`/`carousel`, only the z-index bump is
118	 *          needed here — plus `cursor: 'pointer'`, since this element is no longer inside the
119	 *          `<a>` that used to convey that affordance via the browser's default link cursor. Fixing
120	 *          this the same way used to fix `close`/`carousel` necessarily breaks the accidental
121	 *          click-still-navigates behaviour described above (media no longer lets the click reach
122	 *          the overlay at all) — restored deliberately via a real `onClick` on
123	 *          `ZimmProductCardMedia` instead of relying on the overlay by accident: see index.tsx's
124	 *          own docblock for the click-passthrough narrative, and its `handleMediaClick`, which
125	 *          guards the two arrow buttons and the remove/close button (all real `<button>`
126	 *          descendants of `media`) so they keep doing only their own thing.
127	 *   3. THE HOVER-REVEAL SWAP between price and the PLP/Wishlist size-selector (and Home's
128	 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
129	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
130	 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:has(:focus-visible)` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below,
131	 *      superseded by Fix H — see point 6) — `:hover` alone would leave every reveal permanently
132	 *      unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable device.

473	          // engine but still matches genuine Tab navigation — so the keyboard case Fix 2 exists
474	          // for keeps working, and the mouse-click case that produced the stuck-open bug does
475	          // not. `:has()` is not used anywhere else in this codebase yet; it is fully covered by
476	          // this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`, `last 4 ChromeAndroid
477	          // versions`), all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 shipping baseline. Expressed as a
478	          // separate string key (not a comma-joined `'&:hover, &:has(:focus-visible) ...'`
479	          // selector) to match this file's own established idiom; raw selector strings are used
480	          // throughout rather than a Chakra shorthand prop because the descendant-combinator
481	          // path has to be baked into the selector itself, and Chakra has no `:has()` shorthand.
482	          // Fix J: was `display: 'block'` — converted alongside the `&:hover` entry above; see
483	          // docblock point 3/6 for why `display` no longer expresses this at all.
484	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
485	            position: 'static',
486	            clipPath: 'none',
487	          },
488	        }),
489	        ...(hoverHidesPrice && {
490	          // PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default (no unconditional rule needed above) and
491	          // hides only here, in favour of the size-selector reveal alongside it. Fix J: both
492	          // entries below were `display: 'none'` — see docblock point 3/6.
493	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
494	            position: 'absolute',
495	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
496	          },
497	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
498	          // Keyboard focus anywhere in the card must hide price in favour of the size-selector
499	          // exactly as hover does, so a keyboard user sees the identical revealed state, not a
500	          // different partial one; `:has(:focus-visible)` keeps that true while no longer
501	          // sticking open after a mouse click.
502	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
503	            position: 'absolute',
504	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
505	          },
506	        }),
507	        ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
508	          // Fix K (see the unconditional block above for the full narrative): a hover-capable
509	          // pointer overrides the `display: 'none'` above with the Fix J clip-path technique —
510	          // this pointer type genuinely CAN reveal the content below, so it needs to stay in the
511	          // DOM/tab order while merely not-yet-revealed, for the same VoiceOver/AT reason Fix J
512	          // exists at all. `display: 'flex'` matches ZimmSizeChipGroup's own natural root display
513	          // (zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts's `radiogroup`/`oneSize` parts) — `position`/`clipPath` are
514	          // the only properties the reveal pair below needs to toggle.
515	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
516	            display: 'flex',
517	            position: 'absolute',
518	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
519	          },
520	          // ...and is only revealed here, matching the price swap alongside it. Fix J: both
521	          // entries below were `display: 'block'` — see docblock point 3/6.
522	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
523	            position: 'static',
524	            clipPath: 'none',
525	          },
526	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
527	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
528	            position: 'static',
529	            clipPath: 'none',
530	          },
531	        }),
532	        // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Both the "hidden by default" declaration AND its reveal
533	        // live inside this same media-query block (unlike price/the size-selector above, whose
534	        // "hidden by default" half is unconditional): a touch pointer never matches this query at
535	        // all, so it never sees the hidden rule below either, leaving notify-me at its natural
536	        // (visible) default — exactly the unconditional visibility every Mobile Unavailable
537	        // reference confirms. Fix J: all three declarations below were `display: 'none'`/
538	        // `'block'` — converted together, same reasoning as the price/size-selector pair above.
539	        ...(hoverRevealsNotifyMe && {
540	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
541	            position: 'absolute',
542	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
543	          },
544	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
545	            position: 'static',
546	            clipPath: 'none',
547	          },
548	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
549	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
550	            position: 'static',
551	            clipPath: 'none',
552	          },
553	        }),
554	
555	        // 6. Carousel arrow reveal — see docblock point 6. Unconditional (no
556	        // `ZimmProductCardStyleProps` flag gates it): desktop prev/next arrows behave identically
557	        // across every variation whenever a card has more than one image. Confirmed against the
558	        // Jira AC ("when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear") and live Figma:
559	        // the Carousel element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance checked, visible
560	        // only on the matching Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist.
561	        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: { display: 'flex' }` used to
562	        // reveal this permanently on any hover-capable device (a device-capability check, not an
563	        // actual-hover one) — removed entirely there; this pair is now the only reveal path left,
564	        // the same `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` shape as the price/size-selector swap above.
565	        // Fix J: `display: 'flex'` stays here (unlike the other four sites' reveal rules, which
566	        // drop `display` entirely) — `clipPath: 'none'` is ADDED alongside it, not instead of it.
567	        // See docblock point 6's own Fix J note for why: this part needs `display: flex` for its
568	        // own `justifyContent`/`alignItems` layout, and nothing else asserts that once
569	        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own unconditional `display: 'none'` is replaced by
570	        // `clipPath`. `position` is deliberately absent from both entries below, also unlike the
571	        // other four sites: this part is `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally already (Media's
572	        // own vertical-centring rule), and toggling it to `'static'` here would break that
573	        // centring the instant the arrows are revealed.
574	        //
575	        // Fix K (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a hover-capable
576	        // pointer needs its OWN not-yet-revealed base state here — `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s
577	        // own `carousel` part reverted to an unconditional `display: 'none'` (Fix K there), which a
578	        // hover-capable pointer must override to `flex`/clipped before `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`
579	        // below can reveal it at all; without this, the arrows never render even on desktop. Touch
580	        // pointers never enter this media query, so they correctly keep the unconditional
581	        // `display: 'none'` and never become tab stops for a control they can never reveal.
582	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
583	          display: 'flex',
584	          clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
585	        },
586	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
587	          display: 'flex',
588	          clipPath: 'none',
589	        },
590	        // Fix J belt-and-braces (see docblock point 6 and the new lift-adjacent rule in point 2
591	        // above): re-enables the arrow buttons' hit-testing only once genuinely revealed.
592	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
593	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
594	        },
595	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
596	          display: 'flex',
597	          clipPath: 'none',
598	        },
599	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
600	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
601	        },
602	      },
603	
604	      // 5. PLP-only bag-icon mobile hide — see docblock point 5. A separate, sibling media-query
605	      // key from HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY above (a viewport-width gate, not a pointer-capability one).
606	      // Mobile-first: hidden by default, shown again from the shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below.
607	      ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
608	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
609	      }),
610	
611	      // Fix F+D's shared desktop-reveal block — deliberately ONE `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key,
612	      // not two. A first version of this recipe gave `sizeSelectorUnavailable` and
613	      // `hideBagOnMobile` each their OWN separate `...(condition && { [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {...} })`
614	      // spread (mirroring how every other flag in this file gets its own independent spread) —
615	      // which silently broke, because both spreads produce a property with the exact same
616	      // *computed key string* (`'@media (min-width: 48em)'`) on the same `root` object. Object
617	      // spread is a SHALLOW merge: it does not deep-merge two spreads that happen to share a key,
618	      // it just lets whichever spread comes LAST overwrite the earlier one's value entirely. With
619	      // `hideBagOnMobile`'s spread positioned after `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s in this file, its
620	      // `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object silently replaced the other's, and the price-reveal-on-desktop
621	      // rule vanished from the actual emitted CSS — confirmed for real via
622	      // `document.styleSheets` in a live browser (price stayed `display: none` at 1280px width
623	      // despite `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 48em)').matches` correctly reporting `true`);
624	      // every jsdom test still passed, because each one only ever sets ONE of the two colliding
625	      // flags at a time, never the realistic combination a genuine unavailable PLP card produces.
626	      // `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` above never had this problem because it was always written as a
627	      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows
628	      // that same shape.
629	      [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {
630	        ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
631	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'block' },
632	        }),
633	        ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
634	          // 'flex', not 'block': ZimmProductCardContent's own `bagWrapper` part sets
635	          // `display: 'flex'` (it centres the icon inside via alignItems/justifyContent) — this
636	          // organism's `[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="bag"]` selector has higher
637	          // specificity (a class + two attribute selectors vs. Content's own single class) and
638	          // would win the cascade either way, so restoring the actual display type Content uses
639	          // matters here, not just "anything visible" — 'block' would silently flatten that
640	          // wrapper's centering.
641	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
642	        }),
643	      },
644	    },
645	  }),
646	};

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { CARD_SLOT, HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY, DESKTOP_QUERY } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';

/**
 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
 * arrows/indicator split — now a shared import from `zimmProductCardShared.ts` rather than each
 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the
 * exact same media feature, on this shared root.
 */

/**
 * A viewport-width gate, unrelated to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above — governs the PLP-only bag-icon
 * mobile hide (Fix D, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) below. Also a shared import from
 * `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, same reasoning as `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above: this and
 * `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own `root` padding step both need the identical `min-width`
 * gate, and a module-private copy in each file was exactly the drift risk this extraction removes.
 */

type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */
  hoverRevealsPrice?: boolean;
  /** PLP + Wishlist — price is visible by default (Content's own natural rendering; no override
   *  needed for that half) and hides only once a hover-capable pointer hovers the card. */
  hoverHidesPrice?: boolean;
  /** PLP + Wishlist — the size-chip picker is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default
   *  and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card, in the same
   *  media-query gate as the price swap above so both engage together. */
  hoverRevealsSizeSelector?: boolean;
  /** Fix C — true whenever ZimmProductCardContent actually mounted a notify-me button
   *  (`isUnavailable && onNotifyMe`, computed once in index.tsx as `showNotifyMe`). Unlike the two
   *  flags above, the "hidden by default" half lives INSIDE `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, not outside it
   *  — see docblock point 4: a touch pointer must see notify-me unconditionally (confirmed via
   *  every Mobile Unavailable Figma reference), where price/the size-selector do the opposite. */
  hoverRevealsNotifyMe?: boolean;
  /** Fix C — true for a PLP/Wishlist card that would normally hover-swap to the size-selector
   *  (`config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector`) but is out of stock. Unlike every other flag here, this
   *  is not a pointer-type concern at all: the size-chip wrapper stays hidden permanently, in
   *  every state, on every device — see docblock point 4. */
  sizeSelectorUnavailable?: boolean;
  /** Fix D — PLP only (`VARIATION_CONFIG.plp.hideBagOnMobile` in index.tsx). A viewport-width
   *  concern, not a pointer-type one: hidden below `breakpoints.md`, visible from it up — see
   *  docblock point 5. */
  hideBagOnMobile?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
 * own by itself:
 *
 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
 *      Four separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but four plain keys need no such
 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
 *      ONE of the four (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close`, `carousel`, and `media` are the three
 *      exceptions: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own recipe already positions each of them directly
 *      (`close` via `position: absolute, top: 0, right: 0`; `carousel` via `position: absolute,
 *      top: 50%, ...`; `media` — its own root — via `position: relative`), so each needs (and
 *      gets) only the z-index bump here:
 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the
 *          round-2 Scorer PASS, which explicitly flagged that check as still outstanding, not by
 *          any automated pass). The lift rule used to target
 *          `'[data-card-slot="carousel"] button'` — the two arrow BUTTONS individually, each given
 *          its own `position: relative, zIndex: 1` — identical in shape to the `content button`
 *          rule above, and every jsdom test passed. A real click in a real browser still landed on
 *          the overlay, not the arrow. Root cause: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `carousel` part
 *          sets `transform: translateY(-50%)` (to vertically centre the arrow row against `slide`),
 *          and `transform` unconditionally creates a NEW stacking context on that element,
 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles
 *          against the *other* arrow button, never against anything outside `carousel` (like the
 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.
 *        - `media` — Fix I (SFCC-236, found via a real mobile-device touch-swipe check performed
 *          after this branch's own live testing round, not by any automated pass). The media/
 *          gallery scroll region itself was never added to this lift list, even though it is
 *          exactly as interactive as the controls nested inside it: with no z-index of its own,
 *          `[data-card-slot="media"]` sat at the same default/auto stacking layer the overlay
 *          itself occupies, so a touch swipe starting on the image landed on the invisible
 *          overlay `<a>` first and the real scroll container underneath never received the
 *          gesture — the slide indicator still rendered correctly (proving the image data/gallery
 *          logic was fine), but nothing paged. Missed earlier because `close`/`carousel`/content-
 *          buttons were each checked with a real CLICK (Fix 1, Fix 3 above) — and a click on the
 *          image happened to "work" by accident either way, since it also landed on the overlay
 *          `<a>` and still navigated to the PDP — so nothing about a plain tap ever surfaced this;
 *          only a real SWIPE (which needs the scroll container itself, not the overlay, to be the
 *          hit target) exposed the gap. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own root is already `position:
 *          relative` (its own recipe), so, same as `close`/`carousel`, only the z-index bump is
 *          needed here — plus `cursor: 'pointer'`, since this element is no longer inside the
 *          `<a>` that used to convey that affordance via the browser's default link cursor. Fixing
 *          this the same way used to fix `close`/`carousel` necessarily breaks the accidental
 *          click-still-navigates behaviour described above (media no longer lets the click reach
 *          the overlay at all) — restored deliberately via a real `onClick` on
 *          `ZimmProductCardMedia` instead of relying on the overlay by accident: see index.tsx's
 *          own docblock for the click-passthrough narrative, and its `handleMediaClick`, which
 *          guards the two arrow buttons and the remove/close button (all real `<button>`
 *          descendants of `media`) so they keep doing only their own thing.
 *   3. THE HOVER-REVEAL SWAP between price and the PLP/Wishlist size-selector (and Home's
 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:has(:focus-visible)` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below,
 *      superseded by Fix H — see point 6) — `:hover` alone would leave every reveal permanently
 *      unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable device.
 *
 *      Fix J (SFCC-236, this fix — full defect + fix write-up lives at the end of point 6):
 *      "hidden" and "revealed" are expressed via `position`/`clipPath`, not `display`, at every
 *      site in this block. `display: 'none'` used to mean "hidden" here, but `display: none`
 *      unconditionally strips an element from the accessibility tree, not just from paint — see
 *      point 6's own Fix J note for the full defect this caused. Hidden is now `position:
 *      'absolute', clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` (out of flow, paints nothing — identical visual/layout
 *      footprint to `display: none` — but stays in the DOM, tab order, and accessibility tree);
 *      revealed is `position: 'static', clipPath: 'none'` (back in normal flow, painted again) —
 *      the exact technique `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` already ships for its own off-page
 *      swatches. The trigger selectors themselves (`:hover`, `:has(:focus-visible)`) are
 *      byte-for-byte unchanged by Fix J — only the property values inside these blocks changed.
 *   4. NOTIFY-ME'S HOVER GATE (Fix C, found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit against the
 *      real Figma Default+Hover Unavailable instances for all three variations, desktop AND
 *      mobile). Three behaviours confirmed together, all different from point 3 above:
 *        - `isUnavailable` suppresses the PLP/Wishlist size-selector swap entirely (index.tsx
 *          AND-s `hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` with `!isUnavailable` before they
 *          ever reach this recipe) — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price
 *          stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own `hoverRevealsPrice` is
 *          untouched by this — its Unavailable Hover reference still reveals price normally.
 *        - Suppressing that swap is not, by itself, enough to reproduce the reference: with no
 *          hide/reveal pair of its own, the size-chip wrapper falls back to Content's natural
 *          (visible) default and would show permanently — briefly shipped exactly that way mid-fix
 *          and caught by re-checking the real render against Figma, which shows size chips hidden
 *          in BOTH states when unavailable, not merely "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
 *          (index.tsx: `config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && isUnavailable`) carries that permanent
 *          hide as its own unconditional rule below — deliberately outside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`
 *          entirely, since unlike everything else here this isn't a pointer-type distinction at
 *          all: every device sees it hidden, full stop.
 *        - Notify-me itself is hover-gated the OPPOSITE way round from price/the size-selector:
 *          hidden by default and revealed on hover **only inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`**, not
 *          unconditionally. Every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it appearing only on
 *          hover; every Mobile Unavailable reference (Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so
 *          whatever it shows is the only state a touch pointer ever sees) shows it plainly with no
 *          reveal needed. Putting the "hidden by default" half outside the media query — matching
 *          point 3's own structure literally — would have made notify-me permanently invisible on
 *          touch, since a touch pointer never matches `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` and so could never
 *          trigger the `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` half either.
 *   5. THE BAG ICON'S PLP-ONLY MOBILE HIDE (Fix D, same SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit). A genuinely
 *      different axis from points 3-4 above: `DESKTOP_QUERY` is a **viewport-width** media query
 *      (`min-width`), not `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`'s pointer-capability one — a large touch tablet and
 *      a small hover-capable laptop window need to agree with Figma's own Desktop/Mobile split by
 *      width, not by input method. Figma's PLP/PDP Mobile Card-content instance
 *      (`40002163:41479`) has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`; Desktop's own PLP
 *      instance and Wishlist's Mobile instance (`40002187:58472`) both leave it visible — so this
 *      is `hideBagOnMobile`, one boolean `index.tsx` derives from TWO separate per-variation
 *      config fields (`hideBagOnMobile` proper, PLP's own unconditional rule; and
 *      `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable`, Fix G's narrower Wishlist-only-when-out-of-stock rule —
 *      see index.tsx's own docblock and `bagHiddenOnMobile` derivation), not a blanket rule. This
 *      recipe only ever sees the one already-combined boolean — it has no opinion on which of the
 *      two reasons produced it. Hidden unconditionally by default (mobile-first, matching
 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own padding step direction), then shown again from
 *      `DESKTOP_QUERY` up as `display: 'flex'` — not `'block'` — since that is the actual display
 *      type `bagWrapper`'s own recipe uses for its icon-centring; this selector's specificity
 *      (a class + two attribute selectors) beats Content's single class either way, so restoring
 *      the wrong display value would have silently flattened that centring rather than merely
 *      failing to apply — the inverse of point 3's hover-reveal shape, but the same "start from
 *      the narrowest/most restrictive case, widen from there" idea.
 *   6. THE CAROUSEL ARROW REVEAL (behavioural fix, confirmed against the Jira AC — "when on
 *      desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear" — and live Figma: the Carousel
 *      element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance checked and visible only on
 *      the matching Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist). Unlike points 3-4 above,
 *      this reveal is **unconditional** inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` — not gated behind a
 *      `ZimmProductCardStyleProps` flag — because the arrows behave identically across every
 *      variation (Home/PLP/Wishlist) whenever a card has more than one image; there is no
 *      `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry for it and this fix does not add one. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s
 *      own `carousel` part used to reveal itself unconditionally inside its own
 *      `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` block — a device-CAPABILITY check, not an actual-hover check —
 *      which made the arrows visible permanently on any hover-capable device instead of only
 *      while genuinely hovering/focusing the card. That sub-block is now removed entirely from
 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`; the `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` pair here is the only
 *      reveal path left, the same mechanism point 3 already established for price/the size-selector.

 *      already handles stacking once the arrows are visible; this handles visibility itself.

 *      Fix H (live-browser check immediately after the above shipped): clicking an arrow button
 *      gives it real DOM focus in every evergreen engine, which kept the then-`:focus-within`
 *      reveal true — and the arrows visible — even after the mouse moved back out, until focus
 *      moved elsewhere entirely (confirmed live: arrows stayed up until a click landed outside
 *      the card). The same shared-root `:focus-within` shape underlies every reveal in point 3
 *      too (price, the size-selector, notify-me), so a click on a size chip or the notify-me
 *      button reproduces the identical stuck-open symptom — this fix was therefore applied to
 *      every `:focus-within` occurrence in this recipe, not just this one. `:has(:focus-visible)`
 *      replaces `:focus-within` everywhere in this file: it matches only when the browser's own
 *      heuristic says a keyboard focus ring is warranted, which a mouse-click-focused `<button>`
 *      never satisfies in any evergreen engine, while genuine Tab navigation still does — so
 *      keyboard parity (Fix 2's original reason for adding a focus-based reveal at all) is fully
 *      preserved, and the mouse-click case is not. `:has()` is new to this codebase as of this
 *      fix; it is fully covered by this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`,
 *      `last 4 ChromeAndroid versions`), all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 shipping baseline.
 *
 *      Fix J (SFCC-236, live-testing follow-up to Fix H): Fix H's `:focus-within` ->
 *      `:has(:focus-visible)` swap above was, and remains, correct for the question it answers —
 *      WHEN does a reveal engage — and is not touched by this fix at all, at any of the five
 *      sites in this recipe. The defect this fix addresses is a different, previously-conflated
 *      question: every one of those five reveals (Home's price, the PLP/Wishlist price<->
 *      size-selector swap, notify-me, and this carousel-arrow reveal) used `display` — `none`
 *      when hidden, `block`/`flex` when revealed — to answer BOTH "is this painted" and "does
 *      this exist for assistive tech" at once. `display: none` unconditionally removes an element
 *      from the accessibility tree; it was never a reliable way to answer the second question on
 *      its own. `:has(:focus-visible)` is itself a browser heuristic for "does this focus event
 *      look keyboard-like," and VoiceOver-driven focus is not guaranteed to satisfy it in every
 *      engine — a real, documented mismatch, and not a touch-only concern: `(hover: hover) and
 *      (pointer: fine)` is true on any Mac trackpad, so a VoiceOver user on ordinary MacBook
 *      hardware is exactly the population this gate applies to. If that heuristic never matches
 *      for a given user, all five reveals stayed invisible to them for the entire session,
 *      regardless of how they navigated — and because these controls only existed as Tab stops
 *      WHILE the interaction condition was true, Shift+Tab entry into the card from something
 *      after it used to skip past them entirely (forward-Tab was unaffected: the always-present
 *      scroll container triggers the reveal before Tab order reaches the arrows).

 *      The fix, applied at all five sites: stop using `display` to express "hidden" or
 *      "revealed"; use `position`/`clipPath` instead — the exact technique
 *      `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` already ships for its own off-page swatches. See point
 *      3's own rewrite above for the price/size-selector/notify-me detail. Carousel needed one
 *      adjustment the other four didn't: this part is `position: 'absolute'` UNCONDITIONALLY
 *      already (`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own vertical-centring `top: '50%'`/`transform:
 *      'translateY(-50%)'`), for a reason that has nothing to do with hiding it — so, unlike
 *      price/the size-selector/notify-me, `position` never toggles for carousel at all here (it
 *      would have detached `top`/`transform` from having any effect the instant "revealed" set
 *      `position: 'static'`, breaking the vertical centring). Only `clipPath` toggles for
 *      carousel. Similarly, this recipe's own `&:hover`/`&:has(:focus-visible)` reveal rules for
 *      carousel keep their existing `display: 'flex'` alongside the new `clipPath: 'none'` — ADDED
 *      to, not replaced by it, unlike every other site in this file. `justifyContent`/
 *      `alignItems` on `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part need `display: flex` to
 *      have any effect at all, and once that file's own unconditional `display: 'none'` is gone
 *      (replaced by `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'`, with no other rule ever setting `display` for this
 *      element outside these two reveal rules), nothing else would ever put the arrows back into
 *      a flex row once painted again.
 *
 *      Two of the five sites' own "hidden" halves needed the identical `position`/`clipPath`
 *      correction, not just their paired "revealed" halves: leaving either as `display: 'none'`
 *      would not just under-fix the accessibility defect, it would silently DEAD-CODE the paired
 *      reveal rule in a real browser — a class of bug this exact file has shipped and fixed once
 *      already (see the Fix F+D `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` note in the style object below for the
 *      precedent, and `index.test.tsx`'s own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock for the analogous jsdom
 *      gap). Once a `&:hover`/`&:has(:focus-visible)` rule stops setting `display` at all
 *      (replaced by `position`/`clipPath`), a separate, lower-in-the-cascade rule that still sets
 *      `display: none` for the SAME property on the SAME element is never overridden by anything
 *      — the element stays permanently un-rendered regardless of hover or focus, and every jsdom
 *      object-shape test still passes, because each one inspects one recipe key in isolation and
 *      never composes both rules through a real cascade the way a browser does:
 *        - Home's `hoverRevealsPrice` hidden-by-default rule (inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, per
 *          Fix E's own placement) is exactly as much a hover-reveal-gated hidden state as its own
 *          `&:hover`/`&:has(:focus-visible)` reveal rules alongside it — it converts too.
 *        - `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`'s own hidden-by-default rule (OUTSIDE `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`,

 *          cascade reason, even though it sits in a different media-query scope than its own
 *          reveal pair. This is NOT the same case as `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s permanent hide or
 *          `hideBagOnMobile`'s mobile hide elsewhere in the style object below — neither of THOSE
 *          has any `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` reveal counterpart anywhere in this file at
 *          all, so there is no paired rule for either of them to silently dead-code, and both stay
 *          exactly as `display: 'none'`/`'flex'`, unconverted, on purpose: separate, correct,
 *          Figma-confirmed, non-regressed decisions, not part of the defect this fix addresses.

 *      **Belt-and-braces addition (carousel only):** `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel`

 *      hit-testing regardless of any descendant's own `pointerEvents`. Now that the wrapper's
 *      hidden state is expressed via `clipPath` instead, its arrow buttons are no longer
 *      unconditionally un-hittable purely by virtue of the wrapper being hidden, so this recipe
 *      adds an explicit `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button` rule below: `pointerEvents: 'none'`
 *      by default (unconditional, alongside the other unconditional lift rules in point 2 above),
 *      `'auto'` again only inside the same two revealed selectors — rather than relying on
 *      `clipPath`'s own hit-testing suppression alone. Price/the size-selector/notify-me need no
 *      equivalent: none of them sets `pointerEvents` anywhere in this file or in
 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`.
 *
 * Parts: only `root` is declared. Everything above is a nested descendant selector inside
 * `root`'s own style object (targeting the composed children's `data-card-slot` attributes), not
 * a separate Chakra part — `index.tsx` never reads anything off `useMultiStyleConfig` but
 * `styles.root`, so `recipeParts.test.ts`'s declared-vs-read reconciliation needs nothing more.
 *
 * `zIndex: 1` below is this file's one deliberately unnamed magic number — accepted per
 * .claude/rules/conventions.md's own exception ("0, 1, -1 in obvious idiomatic uses"): it is the

 * the four lift points, and the stretched-link overlay is deliberately left with no z-index of
 * its own rather than pinned to a specific lower number — so the two sides only ever need to be
 * *some* value vs a *higher* one, never a specific pair.
 */

  parts: ['root'],

  baseStyle: ({
    hoverHidesPrice,
    hoverRevealsPrice,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
    hoverRevealsNotifyMe,
    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
    hideBagOnMobile,

            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          // Keyboard focus anywhere in the card must hide price in favour of the size-selector
          // exactly as hover does, so a keyboard user sees the identical revealed state, not a

            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
        }),

          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {

            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
          // ...and is only revealed here, matching the price swap alongside it. Fix J: both

          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {

            clipPath: 'none',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {

            clipPath: 'none',
          },
        }),

        // reference confirms. Fix J: all three declarations below were `display: 'none'`/

        ...(hoverRevealsNotifyMe && {
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',

        //
        // Fix K (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a hover-capable
        // pointer needs its OWN not-yet-revealed base state here — `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s
        // own `carousel` part reverted to an unconditional `display: 'none'` (Fix K there), which a
        // hover-capable pointer must override to `flex`/clipped before `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`
        // below can reveal it at all; without this, the arrows never render even on desktop. Touch
        // pointers never enter this media query, so they correctly keep the unconditional
        // `display: 'none'` and never become tab stops for a control they can never reveal.
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
          clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
        },
        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
          clipPath: 'none',
        },
        // Fix J belt-and-braces (see docblock point 6 and the new lift-adjacent rule in point 2
        // above): re-enables the arrow buttons' hit-testing only once genuinely revealed.
        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
          pointerEvents: 'auto',
        },
        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
          clipPath: 'none',
        },
        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
          pointerEvents: 'auto',
        },
      },

      // key from HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY above (a viewport-width gate, not a pointer-capability one).
      // Mobile-first: hidden by default, shown again from the shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below.
      ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
      }),

      // Fix F+D's shared desktop-reveal block — deliberately ONE `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key,
      // not two. A first version of this recipe gave `sizeSelectorUnavailable` and
      // `hideBagOnMobile` each their OWN separate `...(condition && { [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {...} })`
      // spread (mirroring how every other flag in this file gets its own independent spread) —
      // which silently broke, because both spreads produce a property with the exact same
      // *computed key string* (`'@media (min-width: 48em)'`) on the same `root` object. Object
      // spread is a SHALLOW merge: it does not deep-merge two spreads that happen to share a key,
      // it just lets whichever spread comes LAST overwrite the earlier one's value entirely. With
      // `hideBagOnMobile`'s spread positioned after `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s in this file, its
      // `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object silently replaced the other's, and the price-reveal-on-desktop
      // rule vanished from the actual emitted CSS — confirmed for real via
      // `document.styleSheets` in a live browser (price stayed `display: none` at 1280px width
      // despite `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 48em)').matches` correctly reporting `true`);
      // every jsdom test still passed, because each one only ever sets ONE of the two colliding
      // flags at a time, never the realistic combination a genuine unavailable PLP card produces.
      // `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` above never had this problem because it was always written as a
      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows
      // that same shape.
      [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {
        ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'block' },
        }),
        ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
          // 'flex', not 'block': ZimmProductCardContent's own `bagWrapper` part sets
          // `display: 'flex'` (it centres the icon inside via alignItems/justifyContent) — this
          // organism's `[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="bag"]` selector has higher
          // specificity (a class + two attribute selectors vs. Content's own single class) and
          // would win the cascade either way, so restoring the actual display type Content uses
          // matters here, not just "anything visible" — 'block' would silently flatten that
          // wrapper's centering.
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
        }),
      },
    },
  }),
};

Author: Marcel Angelo Navarro <marcel.a.n.navarro@accenture.com>
Date:   Sat Sep 5 18:01:19 2026 +0800

    fix(ui-kits): wrap was/now sale price instead of overflowing on mobile (SFCC-236)
    
    zimmProductPrice.css.ts's sale.container had whiteSpace:'nowrap' (correct —
    keeps "Was" attached to its own price) but no flexWrap, which defaults to
    'nowrap' too. That forced the wasPrice/nowPrice spans onto one unbreakable
    line regardless of available width, and with no overflow/maxWidth anywhere
    in the ancestor chain (priceWrapper/root in zimmProductCardContent.css.ts),
    the line painted past the card's edges and widened the whole page on narrow
    viewports.
    
    Adds flexWrap:'wrap' to sale.container, unconditional rather than
    desktop-gated — also closes a WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow gap at high zoom on
    desktop, not just a mobile-viewport concern. whiteSpace:'nowrap' is
    unchanged; it was never the bug. Also adds minWidth:0 to priceWrapper as
    defensive hardening (a flex item with no width property defaults to
    refusing to shrink below its content's min-content size) — belt-and-braces
    alongside the actual fix, not a substitute for it.
    
    Verified: tsc clean, full relevant Vitest suite green (240 tests),
    audit:tokens shows no new violations. Real Playwright probe against live
    Storybook (jsdom can't compute actual flex-wrap layout) confirms the row
    wraps to two lines with zero horizontal overflow once it's genuinely too
    narrow to fit, with no change to normal-width rendering.

commit 2ee4a65f64531b2e9fc95dde8a0c59e9dd6c65f8
Author: Marcel Angelo Navarro <marcel.a.n.navarro@accenture.com>
Date:   Sat Sep 5 16:06:17 2026 +0800

    fix(ui-kits): restore ZimmProductCard swipe paging and hover-reveal a11y
    
    Three regressions found live-testing PR #85's shared product-card family:
    
    - Touch swipe never paged multi-image galleries. The organism's whole-card
      stretched-link overlay was never lifted above the media/gallery region (only
      close/carousel/content buttons were), so a swipe landed on the invisible
      overlay <a> instead of the real scroll container. Fixed by adding the media
      slot to the existing z-index lift, plus a click passthrough (useHistory().push)
      so a plain tap still navigates to the PDP now that the overlay no longer
      receives that click.
    
    - The most recent hover-reveal fix (replacing :focus-within with
      :has(:focus-visible) to stop arrows sticking open after a mouse click) used
      display:none as the hidden state for five reveal sites. display:none
      unconditionally strips an element from the accessibility tree, and
      :has(:focus-visible) is a browser heuristic that VoiceOver-driven focus isn't
      guaranteed to satisfy -- a real regression, not touch-only (true on any Mac
      trackpad). Fixed by keeping every reveal target permanently in the DOM/tab
      order, using position+clip-path (the same technique ZimmColourSwatchGroup
      already ships) instead of display to express hidden vs revealed, so the
      :hover/:has(:focus-visible) trigger logic itself is untouched.
    
    - The touch slide-indicator only updated once a swipe gesture fully settled
      (scrollend), never during the drag itself. Fixed with a
      requestAnimationFrame-throttled scroll listener alongside the existing
      scrollend one.

    fix(ui-kits): wrap was/now sale price instead of overflowing on mobile (SFCC-236)
    
    zimmProductPrice.css.ts's sale.container had whiteSpace:'nowrap' (correct —
    keeps "Was" attached to its own price) but no flexWrap, which defaults to
    'nowrap' too. That forced the wasPrice/nowPrice spans onto one unbreakable
    line regardless of available width, and with no overflow/maxWidth anywhere
    in the ancestor chain (priceWrapper/root in zimmProductCardContent.css.ts),
    the line painted past the card's edges and widened the whole page on narrow
    viewports.
    
    Adds flexWrap:'wrap' to sale.container, unconditional rather than
    desktop-gated — also closes a WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow gap at high zoom on
    desktop, not just a mobile-viewport concern. whiteSpace:'nowrap' is
    unchanged; it was never the bug. Also adds minWidth:0 to priceWrapper as
    defensive hardening (a flex item with no width property defaults to
    refusing to shrink below its content's min-content size) — belt-and-braces
    alongside the actual fix, not a substitute for it.
    
    Verified: tsc clean, full relevant Vitest suite green (240 tests),
    audit:tokens shows no new violations. Real Playwright probe against live
    Storybook (jsdom can't compute actual flex-wrap layout) confirms the row
    wraps to two lines with zero horizontal overflow once it's genuinely too
    narrow to fit, with no change to normal-width rendering.

Author: Marcel Angelo Navarro <marcel.a.n.navarro@accenture.com>
Date:   Sat Sep 5 16:06:17 2026 +0800

    fix(ui-kits): restore ZimmProductCard swipe paging and hover-reveal a11y
    
    Three regressions found live-testing PR #85's shared product-card family:
    
    - Touch swipe never paged multi-image galleries. The organism's whole-card
      stretched-link overlay was never lifted above the media/gallery region (only
      close/carousel/content buttons were), so a swipe landed on the invisible
      overlay <a> instead of the real scroll container. Fixed by adding the media
      slot to the existing z-index lift, plus a click passthrough (useHistory().push)
      so a plain tap still navigates to the PDP now that the overlay no longer
      receives that click.
    
    - The most recent hover-reveal fix (replacing :focus-within with
      :has(:focus-visible) to stop arrows sticking open after a mouse click) used
      display:none as the hidden state for five reveal sites. display:none
      unconditionally strips an element from the accessibility tree, and
      :has(:focus-visible) is a browser heuristic that VoiceOver-driven focus isn't
      guaranteed to satisfy -- a real regression, not touch-only (true on any Mac
      trackpad). Fixed by keeping every reveal target permanently in the DOM/tab
      order, using position+clip-path (the same technique ZimmColourSwatchGroup
      already ships) instead of display to express hidden vs revealed, so the
      :hover/:has(:focus-visible) trigger logic itself is untouched.
    
    - The touch slide-indicator only updated once a swipe gesture fully settled
      (scrollend), never during the drag itself. Fixed with a
      requestAnimationFrame-throttled scroll listener alongside the existing
      scrollend one.

    Two CodeRabbit findings on PR #85, both verified correct before fixing:
    
    - Fix L: handleMediaClick (added when the swipe fix lifted the media region
      above the stretched-link overlay) unconditionally called history.push(href)
      for any non-button click. A real <a> lets the browser handle Cmd/Ctrl-click
      (new tab), Shift-click (new window), and non-primary-button clicks natively;
      this handler now bails out on any of those instead of forcing an in-tab
      navigation regardless of what the shopper asked for.
    
    - Fix K: the hover-reveal accessibility fix (previous commit) kept two
      interaction-gated controls -- the PLP/Wishlist size-selector and the carousel
      arrows -- permanently in the DOM/tab order via clip-path. That's correct for
      hover-capable devices, where a reveal is genuinely possible. But both
      controls' hidden state was unconditional (applying to touch too), and touch
      never enters HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all -- so on that pointer type they
      became permanently tabbable with no way to ever reveal them (a tablet with an
      external keyboard could Tab onto an invisible, inert control). Reverted both
      to display:none as their unconditional default, and moved the Fix J
      clip-path technique to apply only inside HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY, where the
      original VoiceOver/:has(:focus-visible) problem actually lives. Verified live
      against Storybook on both device profiles: desktop still reveals correctly,
      touch's forward-tab sequence no longer includes either control at all.
